experiments.hypothesis: Indian-market visitors landing on motoquant.in don't try the simulator because the hero CTA copy doesn't tell them what they'll get. Variant B replaces 'Try the simulator' with a verb-result CTA naming the outcome ('See your bike's quarter-mile ET') — should lift simulator-runs / landing-visitor.
experiments.implementation_notes: Client-side useSearchParams() in web/app/page.js. Same canonical URL, same href (/simulator), same h1, same meta — SEO-safe. data-exp/data-variant attributes on the Link for analytics attribution.
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if simulator-runs/visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm. Roll back if bounce rate increases >10% or CTR decreases. No decision before 200 samples per arm.

experiments.hypothesis: Pricing-page Pro CTA 'Subscribe to Pro' is high-commitment language that triggers loss-aversion on the click. Variant B 'Start Pro · 7-day refund' reframes the action as a low-risk trial start with the risk-reversal embedded on the button itself, so the eye doesn't have to drift to the smaller caption below. Should lift Pro checkout-init / pricing-visitor.
experiments.implementation_notes: Client-side useSearchParams() in web/app/pricing/page.js. Same canonical URL, same checkout endpoint, same h1, same meta — SEO-safe. data-exp/data-variant attributes on the Pro button for analytics attribution. Studio CTA unchanged (single-variable rule). EXP-001 is on landing-hero so no page conflict.
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if pro_checkout_init/visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm AND razorpay_checkout_completion does not drop >5% (we want trial intent, not abandoned-cart inflation). Roll back if Studio cannibalisation increases >10% (refund-anchor stealing higher-tier intent). No decision before 200 samples per arm.

experiments.hypothesis: Indian-market visitors who land on /simulator see Hayabusa pre-selected, which feels aspirational but disconnected — the 'is this for my bike?' cognitive cost is non-trivial when a 220 hp 1340cc liter bike is pre-loaded for a visitor whose actual bike is a 200cc commuter. Variant B defaults to Pulsar NS 200 (the highest-volume Indian commuter most likely to match a /simulator visitor's actual ride). If the localised default reduces friction, simulator-runs / visitor-to-simulator should rise without compromising the SEO-stable Hayabusa control on the canonical URL.
experiments.variant_a: Hayabusa pre-selected (existing control, matches OG copy + SEO keywords)
experiments.implementation_notes: Client-side useSearchParams() in web/app/simulator/page.js, wrapped in <Suspense> per the static-prerender rule. Variant-aware selection done in pickDefaultBikeForVariant() — name-substring match against the DB bike list so catalog reshuffles (Hayabusa Gen1 vs 2008-2012 vs 2021-2024 model rows) don't break the variant. Falls back to bikes[0] (existing pre-EXP-003 alphabetical-first behaviour) if no name match. data-exp/data-variant attributes on the bike-picker Card for analytics attribution. Same canonical URL, same h1, same meta — SEO-safe. EXP-001 is on landing-hero, EXP-002 is on /pricing — no page conflict.
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if simulator-runs/visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm AND bike_picker_change_rate does not increase by >20% (we want a useful default, not just a default the user immediately overrides). Roll back if simulator_page_bounce_rate increases >10% (Pulsar default may push aspirational-segment visitors away). No decision before 200 samples per arm. Note the SEO consideration: variant A stays canonical because layout.js metadata + OG copy reference Hayabusa; if B wins we still keep Hayabusa as the explicit ?variant=A path so search-result CTR isn't disrupted by the default flip.

experiments.hypothesis: Blog readers who reach the 2nd H2 of a long-form physics post are at a natural mid-scroll section break and have already invested ~3 minutes of reading attention. The current end-of-post CTA fires only after they finish — by which point they are mentally exiting. Placing a pull-quote-style simulator CTA after the 2nd H2 (with copy + href identical to the end-of-post card so placement is the only variable) should lift simulator-runs / blog-post-visitor without cannibalising the end-of-post CTA, because mid-scroll click-throughs come from a reader cohort that would otherwise have bounced before the article end.
experiments.variant_a: End-of-post CTA only (existing pattern — single card after final paragraph)
experiments.variant_b: End-of-post CTA + pull-quote-style inline CTA after 2nd H2 (mid-scroll)
experiments.implementation_notes: Client-side useSearchParams() in web/app/blog/the-physics-of-a-perfect-launch/InlineSimCta.js, wrapped in <Suspense> per the static-prerender rule (page.js stays a server component so metadata + OG tags still flow through SSG). Variant A renders a hidden span placeholder so the DOM tree is identical except for the inline CTA block itself — no layout shift on control. Variant B injects the CTA after the 2nd H2 (block-counter in the Prose function). Same canonical URL, same h1, same meta — SEO-safe. Inline CTA copy + href deliberately match the end-of-post card so the only variable is placement. data-exp/data-variant attributes on both the wrapper div and the Link element for analytics attribution. End-of-post CTA unchanged on both arms (additive test). EXP-001 is on landing-hero, EXP-002 on /pricing, EXP-003 on /simulator — no page conflict.
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if simulator-runs/blog-post-visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm AND end-of-post CTA absolute CTR does not drop >25% (we want net new clicks, not redistributed clicks — if mid-scroll cannibalises end-of-post entirely we have not actually lifted the page). Roll back if scroll_depth_pct drops >10% (inline CTA causing premature exits) or post_dwell_time_s drops >15% (CTA disrupting reading flow). No decision before 200 samples per arm. If B wins, replicate the pattern across the other 7 blog posts in a follow-up rollout (one post at a time so each replication is its own micro-validation, not a blanket assumption).

experiments.element: Pro tier tag-line (the descriptor under the price)
experiments.hypothesis: Visitors who reach /pricing after running a free simulation already know they want more capability — what they are evaluating is 'will Pro tell me something I can act on?' The current Pro tag line 'Everything you need to go faster' is aspirational but non-specific; it could describe any racing product. Variant B replaces it with a line that names the three specific analytical outputs unique to Pro (unlimited sims, ROI per part, build optimizer) and frames them as a decision tool ('know what each mod does before you buy it'). If specificity reduces the 'is this worth ₹499?' hesitation, pro_checkout_init / pricing_visitor should rise.
experiments.variant_a: Everything you need to go faster.
experiments.variant_b: Unlimited sims, ROI per part, build optimizer — know what each mod does before you buy it.
experiments.implementation_notes:
Client-side useSearchParams() in web/app/pricing/page.js, inside the existing PricingPageInner component which is already wrapped in per the static-prerender rule. Uses a dedicated query param ?exp5=B (not ?variant=B which is owned by EXP-002) so both experiments can be toggled independently without arm contamination — a visitor at ?variant=B&exp5=B gets Pro button variant B + tag line variant B; at ?variant=B alone they get Pro button variant B + tag line control; etc. data-exp='EXP-005' + data-variant={exp5Variant} on the

element for analytics attribution. Control is byte-identical at the default URL (/pricing with no query params). Same canonical URL, same h1, same meta — SEO-safe. EXP-002 covers the Pro button; EXP-005 covers the tag line; no copy overlap.
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if pro_checkout_init/visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm AND razorpay_checkout_completion does not drop >5% (specificity should convert intent, not just inflate clicks). Roll back if studio_cta_cannibalisation_rate increases >10% (specificity may push mid-tier visitors toward Studio, which is a good outcome — but only if Studio conversion also rises, otherwise the effect is cannibalisation not uplift). If both EXP-002 and EXP-005 are running concurrently, use separate ?variant and ?exp5 params for attribution; analyse arms independently before declaring interaction effects. No decision before 200 samples per arm.

experiments.element: end-of-grid simulator CTA card on the blog index
experiments.hypothesis: The blog index renders 22 post cards and ends. Visitors who scroll the full grid are high-intent (they came to learn drag racing physics) but the page offers no terminal action — they either click a post or bounce. Adding a grid-aligned simulator CTA card after the last post should capture the cohort of visitors who finished scanning the list without finding a post that grabbed them, converting otherwise-bounced traffic into /simulator runs. Placement-only test: copy + href are fixed across arms so we are not confounding presence with messaging.
experiments.variant_a: No terminal CTA — post grid ends, footer follows (existing control)
experiments.variant_b: End-of-grid CTA card pinned below the post grid: 'Stop reading. Run the numbers on your bike.' → /simulator
experiments.implementation_notes: Server-component blog/page.js stays SSG-rendered (metadata + canonical preserved). The variant-aware CTA lives in web/app/blog/EndOfBlogIndexCta.js as a client component (useSearchParams) wrapped in <Suspense fallback={null}> per the Vercel static-prerender rule. Variant A renders a hidden span so the DOM is byte-equivalent to the pre-EXP-006 control above the footer line. Variant B renders a single full-width orange-bordered CTA card after the grid closes — does not occupy a grid cell so it does not change the post layout on any breakpoint. data-exp='EXP-006' + data-variant attributes on both the wrapper div and the Link element for analytics attribution. Same canonical URL, same h1, same meta — SEO-safe. EXP-001 on landing-hero, EXP-002 + EXP-005 on /pricing, EXP-003 on /simulator, EXP-004 on /blog/the-physics-of-a-perfect-launch (post body, not index) — no page conflict.
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if simulator-runs/blog-index-visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm AND blog_post_click_through_rate does not drop >10% (we want net new conversions to /simulator, not cannibalisation of post reads — if visitors abandon the post grid entirely for the CTA, content engagement collapses and the blog stops doing its SEO job). Roll back if blog_index_bounce_rate rises >10% (CTA looks pushy / out of place) or scroll_depth_pct drops materially (visitors see the CTA early and exit). No decision before 200 samples per arm. If B wins, evaluate replicating the pattern on /features and /docs index pages as separate follow-up micro-experiments (one page at a time, not a blanket rollout).

experiments.hypothesis: First-time visitors arriving at /login (especially via the /signup → /login?signup=1 redirect, and from /pricing or blog CTAs) hesitate at the form because the submit button says 'Send sign-in link' — copy that describes the email-delivery mechanism rather than the outcome the visitor wants ('start using the product, free, with no password'). For returning users the mechanism wording is fine; for first-time-signup intent it raises the perceived friction ('do I need an account first? is this a sign-in for people who already signed up somewhere else?'). Variant B replaces the button with 'Start free · email me the link' — names the outcome (start free), embeds the zero-friction promise on the click target itself, and retains the mechanism noun ('link') so the action remains unambiguous. If the value-forward CTA reduces the moment-of-click hesitation, magic-link-request submits per /login visitor should rise.
experiments.variant_b: Start free · email me the link
experiments.implementation_notes: Client-side useSearchParams() inside LoginPageInner in web/app/login/page.js, which is already wrapped in <Suspense> per the static-prerender rule (Vercel App-Router useSearchParams + CSR-bailout requirement). Only the submit button label changes — form action, magic-link API call, heading ('Sign in'), subhead, terms+privacy footer, email input, AuthProvider integration, and ?token=... verification flow are all byte-identical across arms. data-exp='EXP-007' + data-variant attributes on the submit button for analytics attribution. Same canonical URL, same h1, same meta — SEO-safe. Note: the /signup page does a router.replace('/login?signup=1') so the natural funnel into this page already preserves the signup-intent query param; if we want to default first-time-signup visitors to variant B in a follow-up, we can switch the variant resolver from 'params.get(variant)===B' to 'params.get(variant)===B || params.get(signup)===1' — but that turns this from an A/B into a segmented default, so we hold it for a separate experiment. EXP-001 on landing-hero, EXP-002+EXP-005 on /pricing, EXP-003 on /simulator, EXP-004 on /blog/the-physics-of-a-perfect-launch, EXP-006 on /blog — no page conflict.
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if magic_link_requests/visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm AND magic_link_verification_completion_rate does not drop >5% (we want intent-to-start-using, not inflated submit clicks from visitors who never click through the email — if verification rate collapses, B is recruiting low-quality intent and should be rolled back). Roll back if login_page_bounce_rate rises >10% (button copy reads spammy / scammy) or returning_user_friction_signal increases (e.g. existing-user reports finding the page confusing — surfaced via support tickets, not analytics). No decision before 200 samples per arm. If B wins, evaluate the segmented-default follow-up (auto-B for ?signup=1 traffic, control for direct /login traffic) as a separate experiment — do not bundle the two changes.

experiments.hypothesis: Visitors who reach the bottom of /features have read 6 feature blocks and are evaluating 'is this real, and what will actually happen if I click?' The current CTA 'Try it free' with subhead 'Free in the browser. No account required to start.' restates the free-ness twice but never names the concrete first-run outcome. Variant B replaces the button with 'Run a sim — 15 seconds, no signup' and the subhead with 'Pick a bike, hit go. Real physics in your browser — no install, no account.' — both name the action ('run a sim'), the time cost ('15 seconds'), and the absence of friction ('no signup', 'no install') on the click target itself. If grounding the next click in a time-bound, action-specific promise reduces drop-off vs the generic free-ness framing, simulator-runs / features-page-visitor should rise. Distinct from EXP-001 (landing-hero, cold visitor) — this is a mid-funnel feature-reader cohort with higher intent but also higher 'is this real?' skepticism.
experiments.variant_a: CTA 'Try it free' + subhead 'Free in the browser. No account required to start.'
experiments.variant_b: CTA 'Run a sim — 15 seconds, no signup' + subhead 'Pick a bike, hit go. Real physics in your browser — no install, no account.'
experiments.implementation_notes: Client-side useSearchParams() inside BottomCtaInner in web/app/features/BottomCta.js, wrapped in <Suspense> per the Vercel App-Router static-prerender / CSR-bailout rule. The Suspense fallback renders the control (variant A) markup verbatim so SSR/SSG output is byte-identical to the pre-EXP-008 page — no layout shift, no hydration mismatch, no SEO drift. Variant flip touches only two text nodes (button label + subhead paragraph); h2 'Ready to run your first sim?', href='/simulator', and the 'See pricing' secondary CTA are unchanged across arms (single-variable rule: copy bundle, not multi-element redesign). data-exp='EXP-008' + data-variant attributes on the wrapper div AND the primary Link element so click-attribution survives even if wrapper analytics break. Same canonical URL, same h1, same meta tags — SEO-safe. EXP-001 on landing-hero, EXP-002+EXP-005 on /pricing, EXP-003 on /simulator, EXP-004 on /blog/the-physics-of-a-perfect-launch, EXP-006 on /blog index, EXP-007 on /login — no page conflict; /features previously had zero live experiments.
experiments.decision_criteria: Ship variant B as new control if simulator-runs/features-visitor lifts ≥15% with p<0.05 over ≥200 samples per arm AND simulator_page_first_run_completion_rate does not drop >5% (we want intent-to-actually-run, not inflated clicks from visitors who land on /simulator and immediately bounce — if completion rate collapses, B is recruiting curiosity clicks not run-intent). Roll back if features_to_pricing_ctr drops >25% (CTA may be cannibalising the secondary pricing path entirely) or features_page_bounce_rate rises >10% (specificity reads spammy). No decision before 200 samples per arm. If B wins, evaluate replicating the time-bound + action-specific pattern on the landing-page hero (a follow-up to EXP-001, possibly as a 3-way test if EXP-001 has resolved by then) as a SEPARATE experiment — do not bundle. Note interaction with EXP-001: a visitor at landing-hero variant B then features-page variant B sees a consistent verb-result message; check funnel attribution by segmenting on landing-arrival variant before declaring features-page lift.
